trial_court: Family Court, Hubballi; Family Court, Mysore
case_name: Chaitra W/O Sumit Wali vs Sumit S/O Siddaveerappa Wali
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2005. The petitioner filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights before the Family Court, Mysuru, while the respondent filed a petition seeking divorce on grounds of desertion and cruelty before the Family Court, Hubballi.

legal_principles.principle: The jurisdiction to file a petition under section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act or section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act stands in favour of the party who is residing at Mysuru.
legal_principles.held: Admittedly the marriage of the parties has taken place at Mysuru and the petitioner is residing at Mysuru. Therefore two of the factors satisfying the jurisdiction to file a petition under section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act or section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act stands in favour of the party who is residing at Mysuru.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking transfer of a petition has to establish that the transfer is in the interest of justice and equity.
legal_principles.held: PRAYI NG TO TRANSFER THE M.C.NO.107/ 2017, PENDING BEFORE FAMILY COURT, HUBBALLI TO FAMILY COURT, MYSORE, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY, ETC.,
cited_cases: Chaitra W/O Sumit Wali vs Sumit S/O Siddaveerappa Wali on 22 November, 2017

outcome.final_order: The court allowed the petitioner's petition to transfer the case from the Family Court, Hubballi, to the Family Court, Mysore.

use_for_drafting: advising on residency issues in family court
assisting with transfer of cases between courts
